chat-models-messages.summary: Every provider integration is a `BaseChatModel` that takes messages and returns an `AIMessage`, so swapping providers is mostly configuration. Know how `init_chat_model` picks a provider and makes models configurable, what each message class is for, how `content` differs from the standard `content_blocks` view, where token usage lives, and how streamed chunks merge.
points: Chat models take a string, a list of messages (message objects, `(role, text)` tuples or role/content dicts) or a `PromptValue`, and return an `AIMessage`. A bare dict is rejected. Legacy text-completion LLMs take and return strings.

`init_chat_model` (from `langchain.chat_models`) accepts `"provider:model"`, a bare name plus `model_provider=`, or a bare name whose prefix it can infer (`claude...` to `anthropic`, `gpt-...` to `openai`). Precedence: explicit `model_provider` (the string is then not split), then a known `provider:` prefix, then name inference, then `ValueError`.

Each provider class lives in its own partner package (`langchain-anthropic`, `langchain-openai`, `langchain-aws`, `langchain-google-genai`, `langchain-ollama` and so on). A missing package raises `ImportError` naming the package.

Configurable models: with no `model`, `model` and `model_provider` are configurable by default. `configurable_fields=(...)` is an allowlist, and `config_prefix="writer"` makes the keys `writer_model`, `writer_temperature` and so on. The real model is built on each call, so errors such as a missing package surface on the first `invoke`.

Message classes: `SystemMessage` (instructions), `HumanMessage` (user input, text or multimodal blocks), `AIMessage` (model output, also built by hand to replay history) and `ToolMessage` (a tool result, with a required `tool_call_id` and an optional `artifact` that is not sent to the model). In dicts, `user` maps to human and `assistant` to AI.

`content` is the provider's raw payload: a string or a list of provider-shaped blocks. `content_blocks` is a lazily computed standard view with types such as `text`, `reasoning`, `image`, `file`, `tool_call`, `invalid_tool_call`, server-tool blocks and `non_standard`. `.text` is a property in 1.x (calling `.text()` still works but warns) and joins only the text parts.
Standard blocks are not written into `content` unless the model has `output_version="v1"` or `LC_OUTPUT_VERSION=v1` is set, which matters when non-LangChain consumers read stored messages.

Multimodal input uses standard blocks: `{"type": "image", "url": ...}`, `{"type": "image", "base64": ..., "mime_type": "image/png"}`, `{"type": "file", ...}` for PDFs, or a provider `file_id`. Supported file types and sizes still vary by model.

`AIMessage.usage_metadata` is the provider-neutral token record: `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `total_tokens` (all required), plus optional `input_token_details` (`cache_read`, `cache_creation`, `audio`) and `output_token_details` (`reasoning`, `audio`). Totals include the detail counts; `response_metadata` holds provider-specific extras.

Adding `AIMessageChunk`s concatenates content, sums `usage_metadata`, merges `response_metadata` and joins `tool_call_chunks` by `index` into parsed `tool_calls`. The result is still a chunk (use `message_chunk_to_message` for an `AIMessage`); adding a plain `AIMessage` raises `TypeError`.

Common params: `temperature` (randomness; use about 0 for extraction), `max_tokens` (caps reply length), `timeout` (seconds per request), `max_retries` (default 6, exponential backoff with jitter, retries network errors, 429 and 5xx, not 401 or 404), plus `base_url` and `rate_limiter`.

Model profiles (`model.profile`, beta) describe capabilities and limits such as `max_input_tokens`, `image_inputs`, `pdf_inputs`, `tool_calling` and `reasoning_output`, mostly from models.dev. Override with `profile=` at creation or `model_copy(update={"profile": ...})`. A custom chat model must implement `_generate` and `_llm_type`; `_stream` and `_agenerate` are optional.
traps: Chat models are stateless: a second `invoke` knows nothing about the first unless you resend the earlier turns, including the returned `AIMessage`.
`resp.content[0]["text"]` breaks when a provider returns a plain string or puts reasoning or tool-use blocks first; use `.text` or filter `content_blocks`.
Adding `input_token_details["cache_read"]` on top of `input_tokens` double-counts: cache reads are already inside the input total.
An adapter that puts running totals on every stream chunk inflates usage, because merging sums each chunk's `usage_metadata`.
`init_chat_model("anthropic:x", model_provider="anthropic")` sends the literal id `anthropic:x`, since an explicit provider turns off prefix splitting.
`configurable_fields="any"` lets runtime config change `api_key` and `base_url`; with untrusted config, list the allowed fields explicitly.
Bare `gemini...` names infer `google_vertexai` with a deprecation warning; pass the provider explicitly instead of relying on inference.
Without `_stream`, `stream()` yields the whole reply as one item, so time to first token equals total latency.
